best_for: Owners of Creality FDM printers, such as the K1 and K2 series, who want the maker's own slicer with its presets, on Windows or Mac.
description:
Creality Print is the slicer from Creality Co., Ltd., the 3D printer maker, built for FDM (filament) printers. Besides preparing models for printing, it lets you control and watch your printer remotely and send prints straight from your computer.

You can run slicing from the command line without opening the main window, for example to slice every plate in a 3MF project and save the G-code to a folder, with printer, process and filament settings loaded from JSON files. A portable Windows build is offered too, and some Windows PCs need Microsoft's Edge WebView2 runtime first. Testers and developers can talk with the team on Creality's Discord server.

points.title: An OrcaSlicer descendant
points.text: Creality Print is forked from OrcaSlicer, which comes from Bambu Studio and PrusaSlicer. If you know those slicers, the layout and settings will feel familiar.

points.title: Open source under AGPL
points.text: The code is on GitHub under AGPL-3.0. The README notes that an optional Bambu networking plugin uses non-free libraries.

points.title: Calibration and Klipper
points.text: It includes calibration routines, a sandwich wall-order mode, polyhole conversion and support for Klipper firmware.

points.title: Version numbers can disagree
points.text: Creality's site, GitHub and this listing do not always show the same build at once. Windows here is on 7.3.2, which GitHub marks as a pre-release, while the Mac build is 7.3.1.

points.title: Windows keeps the history
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 20 versions of the 64-bit installer, which installs for the whole machine. macOS lists only the current release, for Intel and Apple silicon.

points.title: Linux exists but is not listed
points.text: Creality's README describes a Linux AppImage and its download page links a Linux build, though the same page also calls the app supported only on Windows and Mac. This site does not track the Linux build.
